findings.claim: Removing `_properties as properties` deletes a public named export, a breaking change for any consumer importing `properties` from this module.
findings.rationale: This file is part of zod's published `v4/classic` surface; dropping a named export silently breaks `import { properties }` / `z.properties(...)` callers. The adjacent singular `property` is kept, so this looks like an unintentional deletion rather than a deliberate API redesign, and no replacement export is added in the hunk. Fairly confident this is at least worth confirming against a changelog/deprecation plan.

findings.claim: `_properties` may now be an unused import (or dead code in core/checks.ts) after losing its only re-export.
findings.rationale: If this block is `export { ... }` over symbols imported at the top of the file rather than an `export ... from` re-export, `_properties` becomes unused and would fail `noUnusedLocals`/lint; likewise the underlying `_properties` implementation may become unreachable. Low-to-moderate confidence since the import lines aren't shown in the hunk.

findings.claim: Downstream re-exports (external.ts, the `mini` variant) may still reference `properties`, causing a compile error or classic/mini API asymmetry.
findings.rationale: zod mirrors its check exports across `classic` and `mini` and aggregates them in `external.ts`; removing the export from only one place typically breaks the aggregate re-export or leaves the two entrypoints inconsistent. Moderate confidence, contingent on the rest of the repo which isn't visible in this hunk.
